question: A shopkeeper sells a book at a loss of 60 percent. Had he sold the book for Rs. 150 more, then he would have suffered a loss of 30 percent. To earn a profit of 20 percent, what should be the selling price of the book?
solution:
Given:

A shopkeeper sells a book at a loss of 60 percent.

Had he sold the book for Rs. 150 more, then he would have suffered a loss of 30 percent.

Formula used:

Selling Price (Sp) = Cp + ((Profit)/(100)) × Cp

Cp = ((100)/(100space+space profitspace Percent)) × Sp

Calculation:

Let the Cost price be 100 units

A loss of 60 percent is 60 units

A loss of 30 percent is 30 units

As per the question,

Value of 

⇒ 60 units - 30 units = Rs 150

⇒ 30 units = Rs 150

⇒ 100 units = Rs 500

Cost price is Rs 500

The selling price of the book to gain 20% profit will be,

⇒ 500 + 500 × 20 /100

⇒ 500 + 100 = Rs 600

**∴ The correct option is 2**
